mint.title: How Gen Z entrepreneurs are using startup builder residencies and hacker houses to start their businesses
mint.snippet: "Others, like Hack47 (which describes itself as Delhi's first hacker house), will pack builders into a villa for a month."

you show up with an idea, find people, build something, break it, rebuild it, and hopefully leave with something you're genuinely proud of.
and now you’ve got a bunch of openai credits to help you do it.
if you're building at hack47, you're going to have some serious firepower to work with.

linkedin.text:
the fastest person in the room is often the least productive.
i've started noticing this after being around a lot of young builders.
i've been to two hacker houses, i'm hosting another one right now, and i've run around 20 hackathons.
and there's always that one person who is moving at insane speed.
they're coding at 3am.
shipping every few hours.
trying a new idea every morning.
changing the product constantly.
from the outside, they look like the person who is going to win.
but sometimes they're just moving really fast in circles.
then you'll have someone who looks almost annoyingly slow.
they'll spend half a day talking to users.
they'll question whether the feature they're building even
